blocks.text: Bacteria are very important organisms, not only for the environment but for all other organisms. They have beneficial as well as harmful effects on life on Earth. Among the great diversity of bacteria, many are beneficial ecologically as well as economically.

Bacteria take part in almost all biogeochemical cycles, in which essential elements move to and fro between organisms and the environment. Nitrifying bacteria (Nitrosomonas, Nitrobacter and Azotobacter) and denitrifying bacteria (Pseudomonas) play a significant role in completing the nitrogen cycle. Decomposer bacteria break down dead organic matter and play a key role in the carbon-hydrogen-oxygen cycle. The activities of photosynthetic bacteria such as cyanobacteria increase the free oxygen in the Earth's atmosphere.

Many bacteria, for example Lactobacillus in combination with yeasts and moulds, have been used for thousands of years to prepare fermented foods such as cheese, pickles, soy sauce, vinegar, wine and yogurt. In the pharmaceutical and agrochemical industries bacteria are most important in the production of important chemicals, and some bacteria are used to produce antibiotics. The commercial preparation of animal skins for leather goods also involves bacteria.

Many bacteria can degrade organic compounds very easily, so they are used to remove or degrade pollutants from the environment, a process called bioremediation. For example, bacteria are used to decompose city sewage into harmless products. Some bacteria can digest the hydrocarbons in petroleum and are used to clean up oil spills. Bacteria are also used for the bioremediation of industrial toxic wastes.

Bacteria are used in place of chemical pesticides in biological pest control. This commonly involves Bacillus thuringiensis, a Gram-positive, soil-dwelling bacterium. Such biopesticides are environmentally friendly and have little or no effect on humans, wildlife, pollinators and most other beneficial insects.

Bacteria grow quickly and scientists can manipulate them very easily, so they are used in molecular biology, genetics and biochemistry. Scientists make mutations in bacterial DNA and examine the changes in characteristics; in this way they determine the function of genes and enzymes in bacteria, and then apply that knowledge to the same genes and enzymes in more complex organisms. Scientists also insert human genes into bacteria to produce therapeutic proteins such as insulin, growth hormones and antibodies.

blocks.title: Bioremediation
blocks.text: The use of living organisms, here bacteria, to remove or degrade pollutants from the environment.
